title: Fringe reviews incoming! First up: Midsummer at @Assembly Festival ⭐️...
transcript: My first show here at Edinburgh Fringe was the new Midsummer adaptation by Jeff Whitty performed by Carnegie Mellon students at Assembly Saint Andrew in the Bijou Theater. Now, I love a Midsummer Night's Dream as a Shakespeare play. I think it's one of the most accessible plays of William Shakespeare. And this new adaptation is a pretty faithful adaptation that takes it and just tells it in modern verse. And yet the verse itself still feels Shakespearean in a way, despite the fact that the language is closer to how he would speak today. And I just kept asking myself while watching this, why? Why this specific adaptation? Because I do feel like Midsummer as a play is pretty easy to understand on its own. And this just felt like an unnecessary dumbing down of something that I feel is usually a really good first foray into understanding Shakespeare. That being said, the performances by the Carnegie Mellon students were absolutely fantastic. And it did feel at times that I was just watching Shakespeare, despite the fact that the language didn't quite hit the same way. They also made really great use of the space. The Bijou Theater is in the round and they were all over that theater, which helped because the theater itself has some really bad sightline issues. If you're in the wrong seat, you really can't have see any of the main action. But there was always some other action to see in the venue. I just often wondered if the other action was contributing to the overall story of a Midsummer Night's Dream or if it was just there to fill out the space. I do firmly believe that with any adaptation, the question should be answered of why this specific adaptation now? And I didn't quite get that answer in seeing this, but I cannot wait to see what these students do in the future.
classificationReason: Creator gives a first-hand review of a Midsummer Night's Dream adaptation at Edinburgh Fringe, but this production does not appear on the list of eligible stage productions.
